# Gumtree (11 endpoints)

## Endpoints

| Resource | Params | Credits | Description |
|----------|--------|---------|-------------|
| /search | `query` / `url` | 5 | Search Gumtree UK listings |
| /product | `product_id` / `url` | 5 | Get a Gumtree listing by ad id or URL |
| /product/similar | `product_id` / `url` | 5 | Get listings similar to a Gumtree ad |
| /seller | `seller_id` | 5 | Get a Gumtree seller profile |
| /seller/listings | `seller_id` | 5 | List a Gumtree seller's active ads |
| /search/suggestions | `query` | 5 | Get Gumtree search suggestions |
| /trending | *(none)* | 1 | Get trending Gumtree searches |
| /categories | `category_id`? | 1 | Get the Gumtree category tree |
| /filters | `category_id` | 1 | Get Gumtree filters for a category |
| /locations | `query` | 5 | Autocomplete Gumtree locations |
| /locations/nearest | `location_coordinate` / `latitude` | 5 | Find the nearest Gumtree location |

### Parameter legend

- `a`, `b` — both required.
- `a` / `b` — a `oneOf` group: at least one member must be provided.
- `a`? — the spec marks nothing required, but these are the parameters the endpoint accepts;
  a bare call usually will not work. See Endpoint Details for which combination to send.
- *(none)* — takes no parameters at all.
- A method prefix (**POST**, **DELETE**, **PATCH**) marks a non-GET endpoint; unmarked rows are GET.
- Every endpoint also accepts the `Cache-Control` header (send `no-cache` to bypass the
  response cache — billed at the normal rate) and `Idempotency-Key` (a UUID that makes a
  retry safe; a replay returns the cached payload without double-billing).

## Endpoint Details

_What each endpoint returns and when to reach for it._

### /search — 5cr

Returns Gumtree UK classifieds matching a keyword, about 22 per page, each with ad id, title, price in GBP, location, category, seller type (private or trade), image, and listing URL. Pass a gumtree.com/search URL as url to replay an existing web search (location slugs default to a 15-mile radius unless the URL carries a distance). Price, seller_type, and attributes filters only apply when category_id is also set. Paginate with page or the universal cursor until hasNextPage is false. Feed a returned ad id into GET /v1/gumtree/product for the full listing.

**Parameters**

- `page` *(optional)*: Page number, starting at 1. Prefer the universal cursor parameter. Native upstream cursor param. Send the universal `cursor` instead: the API maps it to this name for you.
- `sort_by` *(optional)*: Result ordering: relevance (default), newest, price_low, or price_high.
- `category_id` *(optional)*: Gumtree category id or SEO slug from GET /v1/gumtree/categories or search/suggestions. Required for price, seller_type, and attributes filters to take effect.
- `location_id` *(optional)*: Gumtree location id from GET /v1/gumtree/locations or locations/nearest.
- `distance` *(optional)*: Search radius in miles around location_id. Ignored without a location_id. nationwide searches the whole UK.
- `min_price` *(optional)*: Lowest asking price in GBP. Requires category_id. Filter on product.price.current if you need a hard bound.
- `max_price` *(optional)*: Highest asking price in GBP. Requires category_id.
- `seller_type` *(optional)*: Restrict to private (individual) or trade (dealer) sellers. Requires category_id.
- `attributes` *(optional)*: Category-specific filters as comma-separated name:value pairs from GET /v1/gumtree/filters, for example common_for_sale_condition:new,vehicle_make:audi. Requires category_id.
- `cursor` *(optional)*: Universal pagination cursor. Send `pagination.next_cursor` from the previous response back verbatim: the API maps it to this endpoint's native `page` (page style). You never construct, decode, or look up a cursor. Omit it for page 1.
- `query` / `url` — at least one required.
  - `query`: Free-text listing search, for example iphone or golf mk7 diesel. (one of: query, url; at least one required)
  - `url`: A Gumtree web search URL, for example https://www.gumtree.com/search?q=iphone&search_location=london. Keyword, category, location, and price filters on the URL are parsed server-side. (one of: query, url; at least one required)

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/gumtree/search?query=<query>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /product — 5cr

Returns one Gumtree listing: title, description, price, images, category, location with coordinates, seller name, and the seller ids needed for GET /v1/gumtree/seller. Pass the numeric ad id or the full gumtree.com/p/.../{id} URL. Asking prices, not sold prices. published_at is not returned because Gumtree only exposes relative age.

**Parameters**

- `product_id` / `url` — at least one required.
  - `product_id`: Gumtree advertisement id, the numeric id at the end of a listing URL: gumtree.com/p/apple-iphone/iphone-11/1515115590 is ad id 1515115590. Ad ids also come back on every row of GET /v1/gumtree/search. (one of: product_id, url; at least one required)
  - `url`: Full Gumtree listing URL, for example https://www.gumtree.com/p/apple-iphone/iphone-11-11-pro-11-pro-max-unlocked-with-warranty/1515115590. The ad id is extracted from the path. (one of: product_id, url; at least one required)

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/gumtree/product?product_id=<product_id>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /product/similar — 5cr

Returns listings Gumtree considers similar to a given ad, typically around 6 rows, each with ad id, title, price, image, and listing URL. Location and category are often null on this path. This is a single page: there is no cursor.

**Parameters**

- `product_id` / `url` — at least one required.
  - `product_id`: Gumtree advertisement id, the numeric id at the end of a listing URL: gumtree.com/p/apple-iphone/iphone-11/1515115590 is ad id 1515115590. Ad ids also come back on every row of GET /v1/gumtree/search. (one of: product_id, url; at least one required)
  - `url`: Full Gumtree listing URL, for example https://www.gumtree.com/p/apple-iphone/iphone-11-11-pro-11-pro-max-unlocked-with-warranty/1515115590. The ad id is extracted from the path. (one of: product_id, url; at least one required)

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/gumtree/product/similar?product_id=<product_id>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /seller — 5cr

Returns a public Gumtree seller: display name, average rating, rating count, membership caption, and last-active caption. Both seller_id and public_id are required; they come back on GET /v1/gumtree/product as product.ext.gumtree.user_id and public_user_id. A missing seller is 404 and is not billed.

**Parameters**

- `public_id` *(optional)*: Gumtree seller publicUserId from a listing detail (product.ext.gumtree.public_user_id). Must be paired with seller_id.
- `account_id` *(optional)*: Optional Gumtree accountId from a listing detail (product.ext.gumtree.account_id).
- `seller_id` — at least one required.
  - `seller_id`: Gumtree seller userId from a listing detail (product.ext.gumtree.user_id). Must be paired with public_id. (one of: seller_id; at least one required)

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/gumtree/seller?seller_id=<seller_id>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /seller/listings — 5cr

Returns one page of a seller's active listings, about 20 per page, each with ad id, title, price, image, and listing URL. Category and location are often null on this path. Both seller_id and public_id are required. The upstream count equals the page size, so it is not returned: paginate until a page comes back short.

**Parameters**

- `public_id` *(optional)*: Gumtree seller publicUserId from a listing detail (product.ext.gumtree.public_user_id). Must be paired with seller_id.
- `account_id` *(optional)*: Optional Gumtree accountId from a listing detail (product.ext.gumtree.account_id).
- `page` *(optional)*: Page number, starting at 1. Prefer the universal cursor parameter. Native upstream cursor param. Send the universal `cursor` instead: the API maps it to this name for you.
- `cursor` *(optional)*: Universal pagination cursor. Send `pagination.next_cursor` from the previous response back verbatim: the API maps it to this endpoint's native `page` (page style). You never construct, decode, or look up a cursor. Omit it for page 1.
- `seller_id` — at least one required.
  - `seller_id`: Gumtree seller userId from a listing detail (product.ext.gumtree.user_id). Must be paired with public_id. (one of: seller_id; at least one required)

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/gumtree/seller/listings?seller_id=<seller_id>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /search/suggestions — 5cr

Returns Gumtree search autocomplete suggestions for a partial query, each with the matching category and a ready-made search query string. Useful for keyword expansion before GET /v1/gumtree/search.

**Parameters**

- `query`: Partial search query to autocomplete, for example iph.
- `category_id` *(optional)*: Optional category id to scope suggestions to.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/gumtree/search/suggestions?query=<query>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /trending — 1cr

Returns the search terms currently trending on Gumtree UK, a demand signal that cannot be derived from listings. Typically around 30 strings.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/gumtree/trending" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /categories — 1cr

Returns Gumtree's category hierarchy: id, text, seo slug, parent, and children. Omit category_id for the full tree. Pass a category id or SEO slug (cars) to get that node's subtree. Use the ids as category_id on GET /v1/gumtree/search and GET /v1/gumtree/filters.

**Parameters**

- `category_id` *(optional)*: Optional category id or SEO slug. Returns that node's subtree; omit for the full tree.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/gumtree/categories" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /filters — 1cr

Returns the filters available on a Gumtree category (price, condition, brand, mileage, bedrooms, and so on, depending on the category), each with a name you can pass as attributes on GET /v1/gumtree/search.

**Parameters**

- `category_id`: Gumtree category id or SEO slug from GET /v1/gumtree/categories.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/gumtree/filters?category_id=<category_id>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /locations — 5cr

Returns Gumtree location matches for a place name, postcode, or outcode, each with location id, name, type, and coordinates. Feed the id into GET /v1/gumtree/search as location_id.

**Parameters**

- `query`: Place name, postcode, or outcode, for example london or B92.
- `location_type` *(optional)*: Optional filter: LOCATION, OUTCODE, or POSTCODE.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/gumtree/locations?query=<query>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /locations/nearest — 5cr

Returns the Gumtree location closest to a latitude,longitude pair: location id, name, type (LOCATION or POSTCODE), and coordinates. Feed the id into GET /v1/gumtree/search as location_id.

**Parameters**

- `longitude` *(optional)*: Longitude. Requires latitude.
- `location_coordinate` / `latitude` — at least one required.
  - `location_coordinate`: Latitude,longitude pair, for example 51.5074,-0.1278. (one of: location_coordinate, latitude; at least one required)
  - `latitude`: Latitude. Use with longitude when you do not pass location_coordinate. (one of: location_coordinate, latitude; at least one required)

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/gumtree/locations/nearest?location_coordinate=<location_coordinate>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```
